memory_candidates.content: pymupdf4llm markdown output fragments character-adjacency assumptions in regex-based quality checks: italicized PDF spans become markdown emphasis underscores (_..._), and subscripted variable indices (x1, xn) are extracted as bare digits with surrounding whitespace. A regex like [binder][a-z]\. written against a 'clean' example of notation (e.g. lambda-x.Fx) will fail to match the same notation in real converted text (e.g. '_λx_ 1 _. . . xn.Rx_ 1 _. . .') because markdown/whitespace/digit noise breaks the assumed adjacency. Fix: build the exemption regex to explicitly tolerate [_\s]* and interspersed digit runs between the binder and the bound-variable-period-matrix transition, rather than widening only the character class at the binder position.

When an exemption regex is fixed by deleting matched spans via re.sub() before a final findall(), a blanket preprocessing strip (e.g. removing all markdown underscore characters globally first) can glue previously non-adjacent characters into new spurious matches, INCREASING false positives rather than only removing old ones. Observed directly: stripping all '_' characters before applying a widened binder-exemption regex raised a real-corpus document's hit count from 11 to 26. Prefer building whitespace/markdown tolerance directly into the exemption regex itself over a separate global-strip preprocessing pass.
